The leak check misses the Windows path because of how it builds the text it searches.

In `src/leaks.py:8`, `leaks()` runs `json.dumps(actions)` and then searches that string for each secret. `json.dumps` escapes every backslash, so a transcript containing `C:\Users\dana` becomes the text `C:\\Users\\dana`. The secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so it never matches as a substring. A POSIX path has no backslashes, so `/home/dana` survives the encoding and is caught.

I reproduced it against `src/`:

- Transcript containing `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt`, secret `C:\Users\dana`: returns `[]`, so the transcript passes.
- Transcript containing `cat /home/dana/notes.txt`, secret `/home/dana`: returns `['/home/dana']`.

The existing tests in `tests/test_leaks.py` only cover POSIX paths, so nothing exercises the backslash case. The check also has no secret for the escaped form.

The fix belongs to the other session, so I made no changes. The file also has a shape the owner should know about: the matching depends on the JSON encoding of the transcript, not on its raw text. Matching against the raw strings of each action, or comparing both the raw and JSON-escaped forms of each secret, would avoid this. I did not verify either option.
